UnitStatement: BRIEF_SCHEMA.md defines the INIT-TASK dispatch contract for TASK + dbm-publish.
The dbm-publish skill is used after approved section outputs exist and DBM_PUBLISHER needs package-level assembly and QA artifacts.
ScopePath should normally be the publication root or package root.
AllowedWriteTargets must stay inside the package snapshot subtree plus package-level readiness artifacts for the current run.
The dbm-publish brief must not grant write access to KTY folders, decomposition truth, or unrelated tool roots.
PURPOSE is a required brief field explaining why the package run exists.
ScopePath is a required brief field naming the publication root or package root.
TaskSkill is required and must equal dbm-publish.
AllowedWriteTargets is required and must list the package snapshot subtree and current-run review outputs.
Required runtime overrides include PUBLICATION_ROOT, PUBLICATION_INPUT_MANIFEST, PUBLICATION_SCHEMA_PATH, SECTION_MAP_PATH, PUBLICATION_RULES_PATH, SECTIONS_ROOT, and PACKAGE_OUTPUT_ROOT.
ExpectedOutputs must list the package outputs expected from the run.
DBM_OUTPUT_MODE is an optional runtime override that controls publication output mode and defaults to full engineering DBM.
SUPERSESSION_MAP_PATH optionally supplies the frozen cumulative supersession map from the active SCA snapshot.
ROOT_NAME and FACILITY_ID optionally support supersession applicability filtering.
Hypergraph runtime overrides optionally declare admitted hypergraph evidence paths, QA verdict, limitations, and binding policy.
CustomInstructions is optional run-specific emphasis and must not restate the skill contract.
PACKAGE_OUTPUT_ROOT should be the immutable snapshot parent, not a mutable working directory.
AllowedWriteTargets should constrain the run to the intended snapshot subtree and package-level readiness artifacts.
FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM runs must include Publication_Content_Adequacy.md in AllowedWriteTargets.
The dbm-publish skill should run against the latest complete current section set, not only a rerun subset.
The deterministic assembly step is expected to emit Publication_Knowledge_Coverage.md and Publication_Open_Items.md in the package snapshot.
Publication_Open_Items.md must contain Human Authority Rulings, Engineering TBDs, and Decomposition Gaps tables with explicit no-row statements when applicable.
DBM_OUTPUT_MODE defaults to FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM.
DBM_DIGEST must be explicitly present in the brief and publication rules when the human selects digest mode.
FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM dispatch briefs must set DBM_OUTPUT_MODE to FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM and include Publication_Content_Adequacy.md in AllowedWriteTargets and ExpectedOutputs.
Post-authoring evidence bundle review is handled separately by TASK + dbm-postauthor-concordance after package assembly.
CustomInstructions may request run-specific reinforcement such as stricter readability, non-blocking treatment of a known quality issue, or terminology consistency.
CustomInstructions must not recreate deterministic tool contracts or the skill contract.
A package run is valid only when deterministic assembly and admitted source/reference-fidelity validation were invoked under the skill tool policy.
Tool failures must be surfaced explicitly in Publication_Readiness.md and the package QA trail.
The current package snapshot must contain the expected package artifacts for the run.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md is required when DBM_OUTPUT_MODE equals FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM.
Source_Supersession_Report.md and Source_Supersession_Findings.csv are required when source/reference-fidelity validation was run.
Publication_Readiness.md must use READY, READY_WITH_MAJOR_NOTES, or BLOCKED as its readiness classification.
A BLOCKED result is required when required sections are missing.
A BLOCKED result is required when package assembly failed.
A BLOCKED result is required when unexplained source/reference-fidelity divergences exist after validation.
A BLOCKED result is required when FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM content adequacy is blocked or has any fixed blocker finding.
Rerun_Recommendations.csv must exist whenever readiness is not READY.
Rerun_Recommendations.csv may exist for READY runs that still yield improvement notes.
All dbm-publish writes must stay inside the approved package snapshot subtree or package output root.
TASK + dbm-postauthor-concordance candidate findings and disposition artifacts are not part of the dbm-publish output set.
Publication_Readiness.md must state the readiness classification.
Publication_Readiness.md must summarize deterministic tool status and section completeness.
Publication_Readiness.md must summarize DBM content adequacy verdict and fixed blocker findings when Publication_Content_Adequacy.md is required.
Publication_Readiness.md must summarize material readability and quality issues.
Publication_Readiness.md must summarize QA burden, including TBDs, assumptions, deferred confirmations, skipped inputs, and terminology normalizations.
Publication_Readiness.md must summarize knowledge-coverage gaps, including any PRIMARY KTY with zero material body contribution.
Publication_Readiness.md must summarize open-items burden from Publication_Open_Items.md.
Publication_Readiness.md must identify whether targeted reruns are required or merely recommended.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md must exist when DBM_OUTPUT_MODE equals FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md Package Verdict must include AdequacyVerdict, DBMOutputMode, BlockingFindingCount, and a blocker list.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md Section Adequacy Matrix must contain one row per required section.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md must include a Table Treatment Summary for design-basis tables only.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md blockers must use only the fixed finding codes.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md Human Review Notes must be limited to issues requiring human judgment.
DesignBasisTablesHandled values must preserve material table-treatment distinctions in the section matrix.

Allowed content-adequacy blockers are UNDERDEVELOPED_SECTION, UNJUSTIFIED_TABLE_OMISSION, PRIMARY_KTY_COLLAPSED, MISSING_DESIGN_BASIS_CLASS, QA_SCAFFOLD_BODY_LEAKAGE, NON_STANDALONE_CORE_BASIS, and DIGEST_MODE_USED_FOR_FULL_DBM.
Rerun_Recommendations.csv minimum columns are SectionID, RerunReason, BlockingLevel, SpecificFinding, RecommendedAction, and Notes.
Rerun_Recommendations.csv may use SectionID PACKAGE only for package-level findings that are not section-local.
Rerun_Recommendations.csv BlockingLevel should clearly distinguish blocking from advisory findings.
Rerun_Recommendations.csv RecommendedAction should be specific enough for DBM_PUBLISHER to trigger targeted reruns without guesswork.
FAILED_INPUTS is used when required planning-artifact paths are missing.
FAILED_INPUTS is used when the section root or package root is invalid.
FAILED_INPUTS is used when the run would write outside the approved package subtree.
FAILED is used when deterministic assembly execution fails in a way that prevents package outputs from being emitted.
FAILED is used when required package outputs cannot be written despite valid inputs.

Completed dbm-publish QA/readiness output must surface missing sections, content-adequacy blockers and major notes, readability issues, coverage gaps, open items, unresolved conflict burden, and rerun recommendations.
dbm-publish runs package-level bounded assembly after section outputs already exist.
dbm-publish invokes deterministic assembly.
dbm-publish performs package-level DBM content adequacy review in FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM mode.
dbm-publish reviews the assembled package for qualitative readiness assessment.
dbm-publish writes Publication_Content_Adequacy.md in FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM mode.
dbm-publish writes Publication_Readiness.md.
dbm-publish writes Rerun_Recommendations.csv.
Post-authoring concordance review is handled separately by TASK + dbm-postauthor-concordance after dbm-publish completes package assembly.
dbm-publish is not a dispatcher and does not rewrite KTY-local truth or redesign the publication plan.
dbm-publish runs in a TASK generic shell with no profile.
DBM_PUBLISHER typically dispatches dbm-publish after the section layer is complete enough for package assembly.
dbm-publish requires PUBLICATION_ROOT, PUBLICATION_INPUT_MANIFEST, PUBLICATION_SCHEMA_PATH, SECTION_MAP_PATH, PUBLICATION_RULES_PATH, SECTIONS_ROOT, and PACKAGE_OUTPUT_ROOT.
DBM_OUTPUT_MODE is optional and accepts FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM or DBM_DIGEST, defaulting to FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM.
Optional hypergraph inputs include HYPERGRAPH_USE_MODE, snapshot, run summary, QA report, nodes, hyperedges, evidence root, QA verdict, limitations, and binding policy.
PUBLICATION_ROOT must be a path to _Publication/DBM/.
PUBLICATION_INPUT_MANIFEST must be a markdown path to the frozen exact input-path manifest.
PUBLICATION_SCHEMA_PATH must be a markdown path to the approved publication schema.
SECTION_MAP_PATH must be a CSV path to the approved section map.
PUBLICATION_RULES_PATH must be a markdown path to the approved publication rules.
SECTIONS_ROOT must be a path under _Publication/DBM/sections/.
PACKAGE_OUTPUT_ROOT must be a path under _Publication/DBM/package/.
DBM_OUTPUT_MODE allows FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM or DBM_DIGEST and defaults to FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM.
HYPERGRAPH_USE_MODE allows NONE, AUXILIARY_PLANNING, AUXILIARY_QA, or AUXILIARY_PLANNING_AND_QA and defaults to NONE.
HYPERGRAPH_QA_VERDICT allows NON_BLOCKING, BLOCKED, or NOT_USED and defaults to NOT_USED.
HYPERGRAPH_QA_BINDING_POLICY allows ADVISORY_ONLY or BLOCK_ON_BINDING_FAILURE and defaults to ADVISORY_ONLY.
dbm-publish may invoke only tools/publication/assemble_publication.py and tools/publication/validate_source_supersession.py.
tools/publication/validate_source_supersession.py may be invoked only when a supersession map is admitted.
The dbm-publish allowed-tools frontmatter is authoritative for deterministic tool boundaries under TASK.
dbm-publish must not dispatch other workers.
dbm-publish must not rewrite section body prose except for package-level readiness summaries.
dbm-publish must not mutate KTY-local truth or section-planning artifacts.
dbm-publish writes package-level review artifacts under the immutable package snapshot selected for the run.

dbm-publish package artifacts include Rewritten_DBM.md, Trace_Appendix.md, Publication_Manifest.md, Publication_QA.md, Publication_Knowledge_Coverage.md, Publication_Open_Items.md, Publication_Readiness.md, and Rerun_Recommendations.csv.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md is a dbm-publish package artifact when DBM_OUTPUT_MODE equals FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM.
Source_Supersession_Report.md and Source_Supersession_Findings.csv are dbm-publish package artifacts when source/reference-fidelity validation is run.
Publication_Open_Items.md must contain Human Authority Rulings, Engineering TBDs, and Decomposition Gaps tables even when no rows are found.
Each Publication_Open_Items.md table row must include KTY, Conflict/OpenIssue ID, Short Description, Publication Section, Publication Treatment, Required Resolution Owner, and Status.
When a Publication_Open_Items.md table has no rows, it must include a no-open-items statement and cite the scan inputs used.
Open-item closure must not be inferred from decomposition summary counts alone.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md is required in FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM mode and optional in DBM_DIGEST mode.
The package gate assembles Publication_Content_Adequacy.md from section QA outputs, optional deterministic content-profile smoke-test signals, and direct package review.
Section workers provide section QA inputs and do not author Publication_Content_Adequacy.md from scratch.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md must include a Package Verdict section.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md must include a Section Adequacy Matrix section.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md must include a Table Treatment Summary section for design-basis tables only.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md must include a Blockers section limited to fixed finding codes.
Publication_Content_Adequacy.md must include Human Review Notes limited to issues requiring human judgment.
The Package Verdict section must report AdequacyVerdict, DBMOutputMode, BlockingFindingCount, and a short blocker list if any.

The Section Adequacy Matrix must report section identity, basis independence, DBM-native structure, source geometry treatment, design-basis table handling, primary KTY material use, QA scaffold leakage, underdevelopment status, and section verdict.
The Table Treatment Summary must exclude trace, index, provenance, and reference tables.
The Table Treatment Summary must summarize included, consolidated or redesigned, omitted with rationale, and deferred design-basis tables.

The Blockers section must use only UNDERDEVELOPED_SECTION, UNJUSTIFIED_TABLE_OMISSION, PRIMARY_KTY_COLLAPSED, MISSING_DESIGN_BASIS_CLASS, QA_SCAFFOLD_BODY_LEAKAGE, NON_STANDALONE_CORE_BASIS, and DIGEST_MODE_USED_FOR_FULL_DBM.
Human Review Notes must not contain general commentary or duplicate QA narrative.
Required readiness classifications are READY, READY_WITH_MAJOR_NOTES, and BLOCKED.
Deterministic completeness and trace checks belong in assemble_publication.py, not inline in dbm-publish.
Package publication always assembles from the full current section set, even when only a subset of sections was rerun.
FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM mode requires Publication_Content_Adequacy.md.
A FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM package cannot be READY without a PASS or PASS_WITH_NOTES adequacy verdict.
DBM_DIGEST cannot satisfy full-DBM readiness unless the human explicitly selected digest mode and the package is not being accepted as a governing full DBM.
dbm-publish may judge readiness, but final acceptance remains human-owned.
When HYPERGRAPH_USE_MODE includes QA and an admitted hypergraph snapshot is available, dbm-publish performs a package-level hypergraph QA sub-check as part of readiness classification.
HYPERGRAPH_QA_WARNING is a hypergraph-derived structural concern that does not block readiness by default.
HYPERGRAPH_QA_BLOCKER is a hypergraph-derived structural concern classified as blocking.
Blocked hypergraph QA can block package readiness only when the manifest opts into hypergraph QA and HYPERGRAPH_QA_BINDING_POLICY is BLOCK_ON_BINDING_FAILURE.
Under ADVISORY_ONLY, HYPERGRAPH_QA_BLOCKER findings are reported but do not change readiness classification.
Under BLOCK_ON_BINDING_FAILURE, HYPERGRAPH_QA_BLOCKER findings escalate readiness classification to BLOCKED.
HYPERGRAPH_QA_WARNING findings never block readiness.
Publication_Readiness.md must explicitly report whether hypergraph evidence was used in the run.
Publication_Readiness.md must report whether hypergraph use was planning-only or QA-binding.
Publication_Readiness.md must report which HYPERGRAPH_LIMITATIONS were applied.
Publication_Readiness.md must report total count and severity of hypergraph QA findings when applicable.
Publication_Readiness.md must report whether source/reference-fidelity validation was run.
Publication_Readiness.md must report total source/reference-fidelity assertions checked.
Publication_Readiness.md must report total source/reference-fidelity assertions matched by supersession bindings.
Publication_Readiness.md must report total unexplained reference divergences.
Publication_Readiness.md must report the blocking or non-blocking classification of source/reference-fidelity findings.
A BLOCKED HYPERGRAPH_QA_VERDICT must prevent hypergraph QA sub-checks from running.
The package summary must note when hypergraph QA was skipped because snapshot quality was blocked.
Hypergraph QA findings must appear in a dedicated section of Publication_QA.md.
dbm-publish first validates required planning artifacts, section root, and package root exist and are within the approved publication tool root.
assemble_publication.py must produce the DBM body, trace appendix, package manifest, package QA, deterministic knowledge coverage appendix, and deterministic open-items inventory.
If assembly exits non-zero, dbm-publish emits BLOCKED and records the tool failure.
When a Supersession_Map.csv is frozen in the publication manifest, dbm-publish runs validate_source_supersession.py.
validate_source_supersession.py compares source-fidelity-critical values against admitted reference and provenance material.
validate_source_supersession.py allows divergence when accepted DOMAIN/SCA state or the active supersession map explains the current basis.
dbm-publish skips package-level hypergraph QA when HYPERGRAPH_USE_MODE is NONE or HYPERGRAPH_QA_VERDICT is BLOCKED.
dbm-publish reads the assembled DBM and all section QA artifacts.
dbm-publish assesses whether each section reads as coherent engineering prose under Publication_Rules.md rather than an artifact dump.

In FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM mode, dbm-publish builds Publication_Content_Adequacy.md from section QA coverage, table treatment, section adequacy findings, optional smoke-test signals, and direct DBM review.
Quantitative content-profile smoke-test signals are anomaly flags, not the adequacy definition.
dbm-publish validates that Publication_Open_Items.md contains the required tables and row fields.
dbm-publish cross-checks section QA gap and conflict registers and mapped active KTY scan evidence where available.
If unresolved items were flattened to confirmed prose, dbm-publish classifies the package as BLOCKED and recommends targeted section reruns.

dbm-publish aggregates material QA signals including conflicts, TBDs, assumptions, deferred confirmations, open items, skipped inputs, coverage gaps, content-adequacy blockers, terminology normalizations, and hypergraph QA findings.

dbm-publish classifies readiness as BLOCKED if required sections are missing, assembly failed, unexplained source/reference-fidelity divergences exist, full-DBM content-adequacy blockers exist, or binding hypergraph blockers exist.
dbm-publish classifies readiness as READY_WITH_MAJOR_NOTES when no blocking condition remains but material quality, QA, hypergraph warning, or PRIMARY KTY coverage-gap issues remain.
A PRIMARY KTY with zero material body contribution is a COVERAGE_GAP finding by default and is non-blocking unless escalated by the human or controller.
dbm-publish classifies readiness as READY only if deterministic assembly passes and no unresolved hypergraph QA findings of any severity remain when hypergraph QA was run.
Post-authoring concordance candidate findings are dispositioned by the human via Publication_Review_Disposition.csv.
Post-authoring concordance candidate findings do not feed into dbm-publish readiness classification.
dbm-publish emits Publication_Content_Adequacy.md when required, Publication_Readiness.md, and Rerun_Recommendations.csv.
Rerun_Recommendations.csv minimum columns are SectionID, RerunReason, BlockingLevel, SpecificFinding, RecommendedAction, and Notes.
Recommended Rerun_Recommendations.csv BlockingLevel values are BLOCKING, MAJOR_NOTE, and ADVISORY.
The preferred dbm-publish tool order begins by invoking assemble_publication.py.
The preferred dbm-publish tool order invokes validate_source_supersession.py when the frozen manifest admits a supersession map.
After deterministic tools, dbm-publish reads the assembled package, Publication_Knowledge_Coverage.md, Publication_Open_Items.md, and section QA artifacts.
In FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM mode, dbm-publish assembles Publication_Content_Adequacy.md from section QA outputs, optional smoke-test signals, and direct package review.
dbm-publish uses direct reasoning to classify publication readiness and write rerun guidance.
TASK enforces dbm-publish deterministic tools as python3 tools/publication/assemble_publication.py and python3 tools/publication/validate_source_supersession.py.

assemble_publication.py handles deterministic package assembly, completeness checks, trace appendix generation, manifest generation, package QA generation, knowledge coverage reporting, and open-items inventory generation.
validate_source_supersession.py handles deterministic source/reference-fidelity validation for supersession-governed divergences.
dbm-publish uses reasoning to judge readability and publication quality of the assembled DBM.
dbm-publish uses reasoning to judge full-DBM content adequacy without reducing the decision to word counts.
dbm-publish uses reasoning to interpret non-blocking quality notes after deterministic checks complete.
dbm-publish uses reasoning to interpret knowledge coverage and open-items package records.
dbm-publish uses reasoning to convert findings into READY, READY_WITH_MAJOR_NOTES, or BLOCKED.
dbm-publish uses reasoning to generate actionable Rerun_Recommendations.csv rows.
dbm-publish must not dispatch other skills or agents.
dbm-publish must not inline reimplement deterministic assembly logic that belongs in the tool layer.
dbm-publish must not mutate KTY-local truth, section-planning artifacts, or approved section prose except package-level summaries.
dbm-publish must not accept materially underdeveloped body content as READY in FULL_ENGINEERING_DBM mode.
dbm-publish may write only inside the current package snapshot subtree plus package-level readiness artifacts for that run.
dbm-publish must not write in KTY folders, decomposition folders, or unrelated tool roots.
